answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, the agent network audits entrants at an ingress wharf using proof-of-space challenges across a verification terrace. Each agent must allocate dedicated physical storage sectors to maintain its identity, forcing an attacker to incur verifiable disk hardware and power costs per clone. This capital burden renders costless agent replication a fable. However, the mechanism heavily favors centralized operators with surplus storage and accelerates drive wear.
